1) Answer

Based on her official votes, bill co‑sponsorships, and formal statements, there is strong, objective evidence that Rep. Alexandria Ocasio‑Cortez values human rights:

- Equal treatment and LGBTQ+ rights: She voted Yea on the Equality Act (H.R. 5) on February 25, 2021, which expands federal civil rights protections against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. The official House roll call shows “Ocasio‑Cortez — Yea.” ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/202139))

- Protection from gender‑based violence: She voted Yea on the Violence Against Women Act reauthorization (H.R. 1620) on March 17, 2021, a bill strengthening protections and services for survivors of domestic and sexual violence. The House roll call lists “Ocasio‑Cortez — Yea.” ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/202186))

- Anti‑discrimination at the border and due‑process rights: She voted Yea on the NO BAN Act (H.R. 1333) on April 21, 2021, which curbs discriminatory religion‑based entry bans. The official roll call records “Ocasio‑Cortez — Yea.” ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2021127))

- Access to counsel for people detained at ports of entry: The House passed the Access to Counsel Act (H.R. 1573) on April 21, 2021 (217–207). The bill’s official summary explains it ensures a meaningful opportunity to consult with counsel during secondary inspections; the House roll call shows passage. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/1573?utm_source=openai))

- Opposing forced labor/genocide abroad: She voted Yea on the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (H.R. 1155) on December 8, 2021, which combats imports made with forced labor from Xinjiang. The House roll call lists “Ocasio‑Cortez — Yea.” ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2021412))

- Self‑determination/anti‑colonial principle: She is an original co‑sponsor of the Puerto Rico Self‑Determination Act of 2021 (H.R. 2070), which recognizes Puerto Ricans’ right to decide their political status via a status convention. Congress.gov lists her as an original co‑sponsor. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/2070/cosponsors?utm_source=openai))

- Human‑rights oversight and historical accountability: In an official February 13, 2025 House press release, she and Rep. Nydia Velázquez urged the CIA/FBI to declassify records on the 1970s murders of Puerto Rican independence activists, framing it as necessary for truth and justice. ([ocasio-cortez.house.gov](https://ocasio-cortez.house.gov/media/press-releases/ocasio-cortez-and-velazquez-demand-declassification-records-murders-puerto?utm_source=openai))

- Independent civil‑liberties scoring: The ACLU’s Congressional Scorecard gives her a 100% alignment for the 117th Congress on key civil liberties votes tracked by the organization. ([aclu.org](https://www.aclu.org/scorecard/legislators/ny-alexandria-ocasio-cortez/?utm_source=openai))

Taken together—affirmative votes to expand protections for marginalized groups, support for due‑process and counsel rights, backing of anti‑forced‑labor measures, advocacy for self‑determination, and a perfect civil‑liberties record—these actions substantively demonstrate that she places high value on human rights.
